questions.text: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
questions.explain: Third conditional: If + past perfect (had studied), would have + past participle (would have passed).

questions.text: She has lived in Muscat since five years.
questions.explain: Use "for" with a length of time: "for five years". Use "since" with a starting point: "since 2021".

questions.text: The report must be submitted before Sunday.
questions.explain: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle (must be submitted).

questions.text: The homework was complete by the students yesterday.
questions.explain: The passive needs the past participle: "The homework was completed by the students."

questions.text: By the time we arrived, the film had already started.
questions.explain: Past perfect (had started) shows the earlier of two past actions; "we arrived" happened later.

questions.text: He suggested to go to the library.
questions.explain: "Suggest" is followed by -ing or a that-clause: "He suggested going to the library."

questions.text: The new hospital is being built near the city centre.
questions.explain: Present continuous passive: is/are + being + past participle, for an action in progress now.

questions.text: You should have told me about the problem earlier.
questions.explain: should have + past participle expresses criticism or regret about something in the past.

questions.text: Neither Ali nor his friends is coming to the party.
questions.explain: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: "his friends" is plural, so "are coming".

questions.text: Despite being tired, she continued studying.
questions.explain: "Despite" is followed by a noun or an -ing form: "despite being tired".

questions.text: I wish I can speak English fluently.
questions.explain: For a present wish, use wish + past form: "I wish I could speak English fluently."

questions.text: The teacher asked us where did we live.
questions.explain: Reported questions use statement word order and no "did": "The teacher asked us where we lived."

questions.text: This is the most interesting book I have ever read.
questions.explain: Superlative + present perfect with "ever": the most interesting … I have ever read.

questions.text: Unless you study hard, you will pass the exam.
questions.explain: "Unless" means "if … not". Correct: "Unless you study hard, you will fail" or "If you study hard, you will pass."

questions.text: The project will have been completed by next month.
questions.explain: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle, used with "by" + a future time.
